scope_history.change: Generalize Kubernetes Secret retrieval for local Docker across all repos. Rename kubernetes-inventory to bortus. Keep a simple scoped security layer.
Permit secret use without exposing values to the agent. Supersedes raw retrieval and per-workload MCPs.

scope_history.authority: existing repository rules and latest task
scope_history.change: Keep current cluster controls and inventory permissions; no live mutations, new tooling deployment, or unrelated restart work in this planning task.

requirements.requirement: One shared MCP named bortus, usable from any managed repo without repo-specific server code.
requirements.acceptance: Two existing repos discover the same server and approved tools; legacy config rollback works.

requirements.requirement: Preserve inventory tool behavior and separate its no-Secrets identity.
requirements.acceptance: All three names, schemas and paginated results match; inventory cannot read Secrets, exec or mutate.

requirements.requirement: Authorize by expiring UID/profile grants; retrieve only exact Secret objects and deliver approved keys.
requirements.acceptance: Expired/wrong/unknown grants fetch nothing; revoked-before-launch starts nothing; approved exact keys delivered.

requirements.requirement: Run a local Docker check using approved runtime env or mounted files; builds have no app Secrets.
requirements.acceptance: Synthetic UTF-8 env and binary file fixtures reach exactly approved runtime bindings; digests and arbitrary overrides enforced.

requirements.requirement: Neither the agent's model nor tools can recover retrieved values.
requirements.acceptance: Caller cannot retrieve marker through tool frames, logs, process/file access, alternate credentials, Docker or privilege takeover; reenforce on real launch context at G3.

requirements.requirement: Bound local runs and return safe results only after verified cleanup.
requirements.acceptance: Concurrent busy before reads, timeout, disconnect and crash cleanup exercised; incomplete cleanup blocks admission.

requirements.requirement: Activate real Secret access only under explicit operator approval after RBAC and trust proof.
requirements.acceptance: One reviewed digest/probe and expiring real grant pass nonmutating smoke; forbidden operations and rollback proven.

requirements.requirement: Verify operating guidance, discovery and clean handoff in OpenCode v2 before application work.
requirements.acceptance: Exact installed version and evidence for tool discovery, natural/explicit skill use, nested guidance, permissions, ownership and fresh-session continuity.

decisions.selected: Extend the shared Veyra launcher and preserve the pinned inventory child.
decisions.rejected: One server per repo or a Go fork
decisions.why: Reuse contract and pin; no repo-specific logic.
decisions.revisit: Inventory protocol no longer forwards safely.

decisions.selected: One synchronous profile-based injection and check; no redeemable output.
decisions.rejected: Plaintext get, .env export, generic destination or shell
decisions.why: Caller's CLI and model cannot be trusted with returned bytes or handles.
decisions.revisit: A distinct non-Docker consumer has an independently verified trust boundary.

decisions.selected: Unix peer UID plus expiring profile grant.
decisions.rejected: API key inside agent context, repo path as authentication, per-repo OAuth
decisions.why: Local scoped principal without managing another credential service.
decisions.revisit: Remote consumers or independent per-session scopes are required.

decisions.selected: Private rootless Docker, pinned image and fixed check for real values; fixtures for arbitrary edits.
decisions.rejected: Injecting real credentials into an agent-controlled build or Docker engine.
decisions.why: App code and engine admins can read what is delivered.
decisions.revisit: An existing stronger isolation domain is approved and verified.

dependencies.input: Actual OpenCode v2 context, user/project config and migration authority
Existing pinned inventory binary, launcher and scoped identity
Existing usable Linux domain, isolated rootless Docker, enforceable egress and separate UID
Named profile, approved image and nonmutating probe; exact keys, names and dedicated expiring Kubernetes identity
Approved runtime/output storage and private chart delivery authority if RBAC changes

assumptions.statement: One local operator-managed cluster and trust domain; no multi-tenant remote API.
Some apps can smoke-test with existing entrypoint and env or file bindings without writes.
A managed repo shares a caller identity unless deliberately launched under a different one.
assumptions.confirm: W0 and W3; never infer scope from repo name.

sources.claim: Existing local launch, pinned child and exact three inventory tools; source inspected, not changed.
Global local stdio registration, namespace naming, permissions and session metadata contract.
Skill discovery, explicit invocation and permission design.
Namespaced RBAC and resourceNames; runner must enforce data-key filtering.
Rootless uses user namespaces and has host prerequisites; real boundary needs verification.
Prefer read-only secret file delivery; env has a wider exposure surface.

visuals.provenance: Hand-authored SVG from architecture and C-1–C-3

cost_model.notes: Planning allowances, not quotes. No new purchase planned. Existing hosting, operator labor rate and power price were not quoted; labor and operating USD values remain unpriced. Image storage estimates are contingent, not admitted output.
